parsed.study_design: Exploratory ethnographic, theory-building multiple case study with longitudinal follow-up
parsed.population_and_sample: Three urban/peri-urban neighbourhoods and their community-based organizations in metropolitan Cochabamba; 69 interviews with 47 informants (CBO leaders, members, and employees), plus nine follow-up interviews in 2018 and field observations.
parsed.exposure: Internal institutional and governance factors in community-managed water and wastewater systems, especially leadership, agreed vision, collective action, management structure, financing, participation, and organizational form.
parsed.outcome: Implementation, long-term operation, functionality, and subsequent improvement of community-managed drinking-water, sewerage, and wastewater-treatment services, including whether neighbourhoods obtained and maintained service access.
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (pp. 1036–1039) reports an identifiable qualitative empirical design using interviews, observations, coding, analytic induction, and longitudinal follow-up across three CBOs. The Results and case descriptions (pp. 1039–1048) link institutional and governance factors to concrete access outcomes: implementation, continued operation, failure to implement, and improvement of communal water and wastewater services. The population, exposure, and outcomes are therefore sufficiently identifiable for inclusion.
